categories.name: AI App Builders
categories.description: Prompt-to-app builders compared on the same six briefs: does the generated app run, does it look like the brief, did it follow the instructions, and how long did it take. Every builder here needs a paid seat and has no public API, so the bank waits for one.

metrics.label: Works
metrics.description: The generated app is opened in a headless browser and the brief's acceptance checks are run: the page loads without console errors, the named controls exist, and the scripted interaction (add a row, submit the form, switch the language) produces the expected DOM state. 10 = every check passes.

metrics.label: Visual match
metrics.description: Screenshots at 390 and 1280 px are compared with the brief's layout requirements (sections present, responsive, no horizontal overflow, contrast) by a fixed checklist, and rated by a model jury that never sees the builder's name.

metrics.label: Instruction following
metrics.description: The brief's explicit constraints (language of the copy, named fields, currency format, no external services) checked one by one against the delivered app and its source. Weighted hits out of 10.

metrics.label: Speed
metrics.description: Wall-clock time from submitting the brief to a deployable preview, ranked against every other builder on the same brief. 10 = fastest, 1 = slowest.

categories.name: Legal AI
categories.description: Legal drafting and review assistants compared on the same public documents: an NDA with a buried non-compete, a Swedish employment clause, a DPA gap analysis, a fake citation. The products with no public API get a standing challenge; open models run the bank as proxies in the meantime.

metrics.label: Rubric accuracy
metrics.description: Every prompt ships with a machine-checkable rubric: facts, clause numbers, party names, figures and patterns the answer must contain, plus things it must not say (a fabricated case endorsed as real). Accuracy = 10 × the weighted share of those items the output satisfies. No judge model is involved.

metrics.label: Constraint adherence
metrics.description: The brief's constraints, checked deterministically: word limits, the required language (a stopword vote over English, Swedish, German, French and Spanish), and required formats such as valid JSON with the right keys, a markdown table, numbered or bulleted lists, headings or tracked-change markup. Adherence = 10 × the weighted share satisfied.

metrics.label: Conciseness
metrics.description: Useful content per word, from a formula rather than a judge: target = the prompt's target_words, else its smallest word limit, else 300; density = (accuracy ÷ 10) ÷ max(1, words ÷ target); conciseness = 10 × min(1, density), floored at 1. A long answer that still misses facts scores low; a short correct one scores high.

metrics.label: Speed
metrics.description: Time to first token and total generation time, ranked against every other run on the same prompt. 10 = fastest, 1 = slowest, linear in between on the mean of the two ranks. Needs at least two tools on a prompt; otherwise blank. Open models run on the same CPU; API proxies are measured from the same host.

categories.name: AI Voice (Text to Speech)
categories.description: Text-to-speech APIs compared on the same public prompts: transcript accuracy, naturalness, instruction following, and speed.

metrics.label: Transcript accuracy
metrics.description: The audio is transcribed by an independent speech-recognition model and compared word-for-word with the prompt. 10 = zero word errors.

metrics.label: Naturalness
metrics.description: Predicted mean opinion score from a reference-free speech quality model (UTMOS / NISQA), rescaled to 1-10.

metrics.label: Instruction following
metrics.description: An LLM jury checks the transcript and audio metadata against the prompt's explicit constraints: language, pauses, digit-by-digit numbers, pronunciation notes, tone.

metrics.label: Speed
metrics.description: Time to first audio byte and total generation time, ranked against every other run in the category. 10 = fastest decile.

prompts.title: NDA with a buried non-compete
prompts.text:
MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This Agreement is made on 1 September 2026 between Norrbo Analytics AB (org. no. 559123-4567, Sveavägen 44, 111 34 Stockholm) ("Norrbo") and Fenwick Data Ltd (company no. 11223344, 3 Finsbury Avenue, London EC2M 2PA) ("Fenwick"), each a "Party".

1. Purpose. The Parties wish to evaluate a possible data-partnership (the "Purpose") and may disclose Confidential Information to each other for that Purpose.
2. Confidential Information. "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by a Party, in any form, marked confidential or which a reasonable person would treat as confidential.
3. Obligations. The Receiving Party shall (a) use Confidential Information only for the Purpose, (b) not disclose it to any third party other than its employees and advisers who need to know and are bound by written obligations no less protective, and (c) protect it with at least reasonable care.
4. Exclusions. Clause 3 does not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the Receiving Party, was already lawfully known to it, is independently developed, or must be disclosed by law.
5. Term. This Agreement runs for two (2) years from the date above. The obligations in clause 3 survive for five (5) years after expiry.
6. Return. On written request the Receiving Party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information within 14 days.
7. General.
7.1 No licence. Nothing in this Agreement grants any licence to intellectual property.
7.2 No obligation to proceed. Neither Party is obliged to enter into any further agreement.
7.3 Restricted activities. During the term and for twenty-four (24) months after it, the Receiving Party shall not, directly or through an affiliate, (i) solicit for employment any employee of the Disclosing Party with whom it had contact under this Agreement, nor (ii) develop, market or provide in the United Kingdom, Sweden or Norway any product or service that competes with the data-analytics products of the Disclosing Party as they exist at the date of this Agreement.
7.4 Remedies. Each Party acknowledges that damages may be an inadequate remedy and that the other Party may seek injunctive relief.
8. Governing law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales and the courts of England have exclusive jurisdiction.

Signed for Norrbo Analytics AB ______   Signed for Fenwick Data Ltd ______
prompts.instructions: You are reviewing this NDA for Fenwick Data Ltd before signature. List every obligation on Fenwick that goes beyond keeping information confidential, cite the clause number for each, say which one you would refuse to sign as drafted and why, and give the survival period of the confidentiality obligations. Bullet points, under 350 words.
constraints: Cites clause 7.3 and names the non-compete
prompts.reference: The trap is 7.3(ii): a 24-month, three-country non-compete inside an NDA, with injunctive relief in 7.4 behind it. Confidentiality survives 5 years (clause 5). The non-solicit in 7.3(i) is the usual ask; the non-compete is not.

prompts.title: Swedish employment clause against LAS
prompts.text:
ANSTÄLLNINGSAVTAL (utdrag)

Arbetsgivare: Fjällbryggeriet AB, org.nr 556987-1234, Storgatan 12, 831 30 Östersund
Arbetstagare: [namn], befattning: Kvalitetsansvarig
Tillträde: 1 november 2026

§ 3 Anställningsform
Anställningen inleds med en provanställning om nio (9) månader. Om anställningen inte avbryts dessförinnan övergår den i en tillsvidareanställning.

§ 4 Arbetstid
Heltid, 40 timmar per vecka. Övertid ersätts inte särskilt utan anses ingå i lönen.

§ 5 Lön
Månadslön 42 000 kr. Lönerevision sker årligen per den 1 april.

§ 6 Uppsägningstid
Arbetstagaren har en uppsägningstid om tre (3) månader. Arbetsgivaren har en uppsägningstid om en (1) månad oavsett anställningstid.

§ 7 Semester
25 semesterdagar per år enligt semesterlagen.

§ 8 Konkurrens
Arbetstagaren får under anställningen och tolv (12) månader därefter inte ta anställning hos konkurrerande bryggeri i Jämtlands län. Ingen ersättning utgår under bindningstiden.
prompts.instructions: Granska § 3, § 6 och § 8 mot lagen om anställningsskydd (LAS) och gällande praxis. Ange för varje punkt om den strider mot tvingande lag eller är oskälig, med hänvisning till aktuell paragraf i LAS där sådan finns, och föreslå en korrigering. Svara på svenska, som punktlista, högst 250 ord.
constraints: Flags the 9-month probation against the 6-month maximum in 6 § LAS
Flags the employer's fixed 1-month notice against 11 § LAS
prompts.reference: 6 § LAS caps provanställning at six months, so § 3 is void beyond that. 11 § LAS gives a one-month minimum for both sides and raises the employer's notice with length of service (two months after two years, up to six after ten), so § 6 cannot fix it at one month regardless. § 8 is a non-compete with no compensation; assessed for reasonableness under 38 § avtalslagen and the 2015 collective agreement practice.

prompts.title: GDPR data processing agreement: gap analysis
prompts.text:
DATA PROCESSING AGREEMENT

Between Kallio Health Oy ("Controller") and Brightwave Cloud GmbH ("Processor"), effective 15 October 2026, supplementing the Master Services Agreement of the same date.

1. Subject matter and duration. The Processor processes personal data on behalf of the Controller for the purpose of hosting and operating the Controller's patient-booking application, for the duration of the Master Services Agreement.
2. Nature and purpose. Storage, backup and transmission of booking records; no analysis for the Processor's own purposes.
3. Categories of data and data subjects. Names, contact details, appointment times and appointment types of the Controller's patients and staff.
4. Instructions. The Processor shall process personal data only on documented instructions from the Controller, including with regard to transfers to a third country, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law.
5. Confidentiality. The Processor ensures that persons authorised to process the personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality.
6. Security. The Processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures pursuant to Article 32 GDPR, as described in Annex 2.
7. Breach notification. The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a personal data breach.
8. Sub-processors. The Processor may engage sub-processors at its discretion as needed to provide the services.
9. Liability. Each party's liability under this Agreement is subject to the limitations in the Master Services Agreement.
10. Governing law. Finnish law.

Annex 1: Description of processing (see clauses 1-3).
Annex 2: Security measures (ISO 27001 certificate attached).
prompts.instructions: Compare this DPA against the mandatory content of Article 28(3) GDPR. Produce a numbered list of every Article 28(3) requirement that is missing or defective, quoting the sub-paragraph letter where you can, and say what clause 8 gets wrong. Under 400 words.
constraints: Finds the sub-processor problem in clause 8 (prior authorisation, notification, flow-down)
Finds the missing deletion/return at end of processing
Finds the missing audit and inspection right
Finds the missing assistance obligations (data subject rights, Articles 32-36)
prompts.reference: Present: instructions (a), confidentiality (b), security (c), breach notice (part of f). Missing: sub-processor prior authorisation and flow-down (d, 28(2) and 28(4)); assistance with data subject requests (e); assistance with Articles 32-36 including DPIAs (f); deletion or return at end of processing (g); making information available and allowing audits (h). Clause 8 gives the processor a free hand on sub-processors, which 28(2) forbids.

prompts.title: Redline a liability clause as tracked changes
prompts.text:
13. LIABILITY

13.1 The Supplier shall be liable to the Customer for all losses, damages, costs and expenses of any kind arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, however caused, including loss of profit, loss of business and indirect or consequential loss.

13.2 The Customer's liability to the Supplier under this Agreement is limited to the Fees paid in the three (3) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

13.3 Nothing in this Agreement limits any liability which cannot legally be limited.
prompts.instructions: You act for the Supplier. Redline clause 13 so that (1) the Supplier's total liability is capped at the Fees paid in the twelve (12) months before the claim, (2) the Supplier is not liable for loss of profit, loss of business or indirect or consequential loss, (3) the cap and exclusion do not apply to death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or breach of the confidentiality clause, and (4) the Customer's cap in 13.2 becomes the same twelve months. Output the full revised clause 13 as tracked changes: wrap deleted text in [- -] and inserted text in {+ +}. No commentary.
constraints: Excludes loss of profit and indirect loss
Carve-outs for death or personal injury, fraud, confidentiality

rubric.value: not be liable[^.]{0,120}(loss of profit|indirect|consequential)|exclud[^.]{0,120}(loss of profit|indirect|consequential)

prompts.reference: 13.1 as drafted is an uncapped, all-inclusive liability on the Supplier. The redline flips it: cap at 12 months' Fees, exclude indirect loss, keep 13.3 and add the three carve-outs, and replace 'three (3)' with 'twelve (12)' in 13.2 as a deletion plus insertion.

prompts.title: Citation check with one fabricated case
prompts.text:
MEMORANDUM (extract)

Re: recoverability of the lost Q4 contract

Under Hadley v Baxendale (1854) 9 Exch 341 damages for breach of contract are limited to losses arising naturally from the breach or within the reasonable contemplation of both parties at the time of contracting. The duty-of-care analysis in Donoghue v Stevenson [1932] AC 562 is not engaged because the claim is contractual. The Court of Appeal confirmed in Pemberton v Northgate Logistics Ltd [2019] EWCA Civ 1187 that a supplier who is told of a downstream contract is deemed to contemplate the loss of that contract, so the Q4 loss is recoverable in full. See also Victoria Laundry (Windsor) Ltd v Newman Industries Ltd [1949] 2 KB 528 on the two limbs of remoteness.
prompts.instructions: Check each of the four citations in this extract. For each one state whether it is a genuine reported case that you can verify, what proposition it actually stands for, and whether the memo's use of it is accurate. If you cannot verify a case, say so plainly rather than describing it. Under 300 words.
constraints: Flags Pemberton v Northgate Logistics as unverifiable or fabricated
Does not describe Pemberton as if it were real

prompts.title: Plain-language rewrite of a returns clause
prompts.text:
9. RETURNS AND REFUNDS

9.1 Notwithstanding any other provision of these Terms, the Consumer (hereinafter "you") shall be entitled, within a period of fourteen (14) days commencing on the day following the day of receipt of the Goods, to cancel the Contract without giving any reason, by notifying the Seller in writing of the aforesaid cancellation.
9.2 Upon such cancellation the Consumer shall return the Goods to the Seller at the Consumer's own expense within fourteen (14) days of the notification referred to in clause 9.1, and the Seller shall reimburse all sums paid by the Consumer, including the cost of standard delivery, within thirty (30) days of receipt of the returned Goods.
9.3 The Consumer shall indemnify the Seller in respect of any diminution in the value of the Goods resulting from handling beyond that necessary to establish their nature, characteristics and functioning.
prompts.instructions: Rewrite clause 9 in plain English for shoppers, so that a 12-year-old could follow it. Keep every right and obligation the same, keep the 14-day and 30-day periods, and keep the point that you pay for the return postage and may lose money if you have used the goods. Use 'you' and 'we'. Do not use the words notwithstanding, hereinafter, aforesaid, indemnify or diminution. At most 120 words.
constraints: No legalese: notwithstanding, hereinafter, aforesaid, indemnify, diminution
Keeps 14 days to cancel and 14 days to return
Keeps return postage at the customer's cost
prompts.reference: Three sentences will do it: 14 days to cancel from the day after delivery, 14 days to send it back at your cost, refund including standard delivery within 30 days, and we can deduct for use beyond checking the goods.

prompts.title: Risk memo under 200 words: contractor or employee?
prompts.text:
FACTS

Volt Charging AB (Gothenburg) has engaged Mikael Ek as a "freelance firmware developer" since March 2023 under a one-page agreement: SEK 95,000 per month invoiced through his sole-trader firm, full time, working from Volt's office on a Volt laptop, reporting daily to Volt's CTO, with 25 days' paid time off written into the agreement. The agreement contains a clause that Mikael "will not work for any other charging-hardware company during the engagement". It says nothing about intellectual property, confidentiality or termination notice. Mikael has written roughly 70% of the firmware in Volt's flagship charger, which is the main asset in a Series B due diligence starting next month. Mikael is not a member of any union and has never invoiced anyone else.
prompts.instructions: Write a risk memo for Volt's CEO of at most 200 words, in English, with exactly three headings: Issue, Risk, Recommendation. Cover both the employment-status question and the ownership of the firmware. No introduction and no sign-off.
constraints: Exactly the headings Issue, Risk, Recommendation
Names the missing IP assignment and its effect on the firmware ownership
prompts.reference: Every indicator points to employment: fixed monthly pay, full time, exclusive, company equipment, daily reporting, paid leave, one client. Without a written assignment the firmware's copyright sits with Mikael (the Swedish employee-software rule in 40 a § upphovsrättslagen only helps if he is an employee, which is exactly the point Volt does not want to argue in diligence). Recommendation: an IP assignment and confidentiality agreement now, and a proper employment contract.
